title: Reading the ice
text: By {{1}} annual layers of ice, scientists read the planet's climate history {{2}} pages of a book. Snow turns {{3}} firn and then into solid ice, preserving {{4}} year's chemistry in a separate band, {{5}} means a core drilled from the deep ice in Antarctica is a calendar counting back hundreds of millennia. Trapped air bubbles, {{6}} preserve samples of the ancient atmosphere, allow temperatures to {{7}} reconstructed for every year they represent. Such was the evidence {{8}} politicians began quoting ice cores in climate debates — the planet, it turns out, keeps minutes, and the ice holds them.

gaps.explanation: 'By + gerund' — the means of reading: by counting.

gaps.explanation: 'Each year's' — one by one; 'each' takes a singular noun directly.
